User guide

How to use Price Truth

A step-by-step walkthrough of the dashboard and the detail pages, with what every number means.

1Getting started

Price Truth answers one question: is the price in front of you fair? The home page explains what it does; type a product into its search box, or press Open the dashboard.

Everything else happens on one dashboard that fills the screen:

  1. Choose the product with the dropdowns: Platform → Category → Subcategory → Product. The product list shows the most-rated listings first; type in Filter by name to narrow it (for example cable or kurta).
  2. Enter the prices you see. Listed MRP is the crossed-out "was" price; Price you see is the price you would pay. Both start at today's price for that listing. Every figure updates as soon as you change one.
  3. Read the six headline cards, then scroll, or use the section menu, for the detail behind each one.
Hover for the "why"Every headline card explains how its number was produced when you hover over it (or tab to it with the keyboard).

2The six headline cards

CardWhat it tells youGood sign
Price verdictWhether your price is below, inside or above the range similar listings sold for. Below expected
Fair price estimateWhat the model expects this product to cost, with the range that holds 90% of real held-out prices.Your price at or below the estimate
Advertised discountThe discount off MRP, compared with this product's usual discount over 90 days.Close to usual is normal; far above usual deserves a second look
Real savingHow far the price is below its lowest price of the 30 days before the sale (the EU Omnibus rule).5% or more
Inflation riskA classifier's estimate that the discount is inflated, judged from the listing alone. Below the flag line
Best place to buyThe cheapest platform today including delivery and platform fees. Shows how much you would save

3Fair price

The Fair price card places your price (diamond) on the model's expected range (box) with its estimate (line). Below it, why the estimate is what it is: starting from a typical listing, each factor moved the estimate up (blue) or down (coral) by the percentage shown. These are SHAP values from the trained model.

Listed MRP mattersThe model uses the MRP as an input, so an inflated MRP raises the estimate. That is why the discount check below exists.

4Discount check

Two checks in one card. Primary: the price-history rule: a discount is flagged when it is advertised as at least 5 points bigger than usual while the price is less than 5% below its 30-day low. Secondary: a classifier's risk dial with the flag threshold marked, and the factors that raised or lowered the risk. The classifier sees only the listing, so when the two disagree, trust the rule.

5Price history and timing

Daily prices for 180 days with sale events shaded; your price is the dashed line. Hover over the chart to read any day. Beside it: how your price compares with the last 90 days, whether a sale is on or coming, and tomorrow's price. The forecast is shown only when it beat "same as today" on held-out days; otherwise the app says so.

6Where to buy

The same product on up to eight Indian platforms that sell its category, ranked by total cost. Delivery fees follow each platform's free-delivery threshold; your own platform uses the price you typed. Use Open to search the platform.

7Pack value

Compare two to four pack sizes. Prices are converted to per 100 g, per 100 ml or per item, so different sizes can be compared fairly. The example compares 400 g for ₹45 with 1 kg for ₹105.

8Shrinkflation

Pick a case to see how a pack shrank while its price stayed the same, and how much the real price per gram rose. Cited cases link to the original news report; simulated timelines use generic names.

9Saving your result

The Export bar at the end of the dashboard: Download PDF report (verdict, range, explanation and limits), Download data (JSON), Download offers (CSV), and a link to the original listing.

10Food & packs

Search a food product by name or barcode. You get its pack details from Open Food Facts, dated shop prices from Open Prices, and a longer real price history example. Compare this pack's value sends the pack size to the dashboard's Pack value section. Switch on Saved responses only to work offline.

11My observations

Record prices you see in shops, one at a time or as a CSV. You then get the price history and forecast for one exact pack, a comparison of your store quotes, and a pack-size change check. Your entries stay in your browser session; download them to keep them.

12Methods & data

How accurate the model is by platform and category, which data is real and which is simulated, every source and licence, and what the app cannot tell you.

13On a phone

The dashboard stacks its cards into one column; the top menu moves behind the menu button.

14Words used in the app

MRP
Maximum retail price: the "was" price that discounts are quoted against.
Expected range
Prices the model considers normal for this listing; it holds 90% of real held-out prices.
30-day low
The lowest price in the 30 days before the current sale began; the fair reference for a discount.
SHAP
A method that splits a model's estimate into the contribution of each input.
Simulated / synthetic
Generated by a seeded simulator calibrated to published Indian e-commerce research, not observed. Daily histories, offers and discount labels are simulated; listings and cited cases are real.
Price Truth · NMIMS M.Sc. Data Science, Group 11 · Academic project. Listings are real historical snapshots; daily histories, offers and discount labels are simulated (see Methods & data).
